text: The Bible was written over roughly 1,500 years by more than 40 authors across three continents.
The book of Psalms is the longest book in the Bible, containing 150 individual psalms.
The Dead Sea Scrolls, discovered in 1947, include copies of Old Testament texts over 2,000 years old.
Jerusalem is mentioned by name more than 800 times in the Bible.
The shortest verse in the Bible, John 11:35, reads simply: 'Jesus wept.'
The Gutenberg Bible, printed around 1455, was the first major book printed using movable type in the West.
The word 'Bible' comes from the Greek 'biblia,' meaning 'books' — a library of 66 books in one collection.
The Ten Commandments appear twice in the Old Testament: Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5.
